monthly_review.summary: This month shows a sharp drop in volume and frequency compared to last month, but notable improvements in pace and aerobic training effect — suggesting higher-intensity focus despite minimal running.
monthly_review.highlight: Despite only 1 run this month, the runner achieved their fastest-ever pace (512 sec/km = 8:33 min/km) with an aerobic TE of 3.1 — matching the highest TE from last month’s longest runs, indicating exceptional intensity efficiency.

goal_tracker.message: You need 54.5 more km across 10 additional sessions (avg 5.45 km/session) over the next 29 days to match last month’s volume — achievable with 3–4 runs/week, including one longer run (≥8 km).

insights.title: Efficiency dip aligns with elevated HR and zone distribution shift
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency declined from 13.46 to 13.2 km/hr per bpm while average HR rose +8 bpm and Zone 3% jumped from 31% to 54% — indicating recent efforts are prioritizing intensity over sustainable aerobic development.

insights.title: Zone 3 dominance suggests underutilization of foundational aerobic work
insights.body: This month’s HR zone distribution (54% Z3, 21% Z4, 0% Z5) shows near-total absence of Z1/Z2 — critical for capillary density, fat oxidation, and recovery. Last month had 53% combined Z1+Z2; now it’s just 6%.

insights.title: Cadence and stride length improved concurrently with faster pace
insights.body: From 6/21 to 7/1, cadence held steady at 153–154 spm while stride length increased from 68.77 cm to 75.77 cm (+7.0 cm) and vertical oscillation rose from 7.7 to 8.1 cm — suggesting more powerful, efficient turnover at faster paces.

insights.title: Aerobic TE is high despite low volume — risk of residual fatigue without Z1/Z2 recovery
insights.body: Three of the last five runs (6/21, 6/28, 7/1) all delivered 3.1 aerobic TE — same as this month’s sole run — yet Z1 time dropped from 24% (Jun) to 6% (Jul), meaning recovery stimulus is missing even as load intensity remains high.

recommendations.action: Do your next run as a 5 km Zone 2 effort at ≤135 bpm (based on last month’s avg HR of 140 and Z2 upper bound ~138–142 bpm for most runners with VO2 max ~39)
recommendations.reason: To rebuild Z1/Z2 volume — currently only 6% this month vs 53% last month — and restore aerobic efficiency (13.2 → target 13.5+)

recommendations.action: Add a 20-min post-run walk or easy spin at <110 bpm immediately after your next two runs
recommendations.reason: To actively stimulate Z1 physiology and offset the 0% Z1 time this month, supporting parasympathetic recovery and capillary adaptation.

recommendations.action: Perform a 3 km progressive run starting at 540 sec/km (9:00 min/km) and building to 490 sec/km (8:10 min/km), monitoring that HR stays ≤145 bpm through first 2 km
recommendations.reason: To reinforce pace–HR dissociation — your 6/28 run hit 533 sec/km at 149 bpm, so this builds efficiency at sub-threshold intensities before pushing further.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish foundational Zone 1–2 volume to improve HR efficiency, support recovery, and create physiological headroom for future intensity gains.
suggested_sessions: 3 km progressive pace run with HR ceiling
